hero.headline: Skilled care, brought home.
hero.intro: Our nurses, therapists, and aides come to you — so you can recover where you are most comfortable, surrounded by family.

pillar.title: One skilled team, seven disciplines.
pillar.body: Your care plan may draw on any combination of these services. Our nurses coordinate with your physician so the right clinician is at your door on the right day.

detail.Stethoscope: Our RNs and LVNs assess wounds, manage medications, and support chronic disease management between your doctor visits.
detail.PersonSimpleWalk: Physical therapists help you regain strength, mobility, and balance after surgery, injury, or a progressive condition.
detail.HandHeart: Occupational therapists work on the everyday tasks — dressing, bathing, cooking — that keep you safe and independent at home.
detail.ChatCircleDots: Speech therapists address communication and swallowing difficulties following stroke, neurological changes, or injury.
detail.UsersThree: Our social workers help families navigate benefits, find community resources, and coordinate the non-clinical side of a care plan.
detail.House: Certified home health aides assist with bathing, grooming, meal preparation, and the daily routines that matter most.
detail.Heartbeat: Connected home devices track your vital signs daily. Your nurse reviews the data and responds before a small change becomes a problem.

specialties.title: Clinical experience across a wide range of diagnoses.

insurance.title: We work with your plan.
insurance.body: Most plans and Medicare are accepted, and we verify your benefits at no cost before care begins. Coverage depends on your specific plan and clinical eligibility — our intake team will walk you through what applies to you.

hero.headline: Caring for Katy families since 2008.
hero.intro: Lifecare Options is a locally owned skilled home health agency based in Katy, TX. Nurse-led and physician-coordinated, we have been bringing Medicare-certified care into patients' homes since 2008.

story.title: Locally owned and nurse-led since 2008.
story.p1: Lifecare Options started in Katy in 2008 with a straightforward idea: skilled nurses and therapists should be able to follow patients home after discharge and keep their recovery on track.
story.p2: Today our team includes registered nurses, licensed vocational nurses, physical and occupational therapists, speech therapists, medical social workers, and home health aides. Every care plan is coordinated directly with the patient's physician.
story.p3: We are not a national franchise. The clinicians who answer your call are the same ones who come to your door.
story.mission: To provide expert, compassionate home health care in Katy and the surrounding communities, so that every patient can recover safely and live with dignity.

band.headline: People heal best at home. We make sure the care follows them there.

values.title: How we show up for every patient.
values.card1Body: Our nurses and therapists meet Medicare and CHAP standards, and every visit is documented and shared with your physician. Quality is built into our workflow, not added on top.
values.card2Body: Home health works best when patients stay in control of their routine. Our clinicians work around your schedule and preferences, not the other way around.
values.card3Body: We communicate directly with your physician and specialist offices. If your care plan changes, everyone on your team knows before your next visit.
values.card4Body: Our team provides care in English and Spanish. No patient should have to navigate their health in a language that is not their own.

why.title: A team worth joining.
why.card1Body: You will know your patients and your colleagues. There are no hand-offs to strangers — the same nurses and aides follow their patients through recovery.
why.card2Body: Home health is not floor nursing. You go to the patient, spend focused time, and make decisions. The work is clinical and direct.
why.card3Body: Clinical decisions stay with clinicians. Our nurses and therapists set the standard for care, and leadership listens when something needs to change.
why.card4Body: We work around the realities of caregiving. Schedules are built collaboratively so you can do your best work without burning out.

hero.headline: Refer a patient in minutes.
hero.intro: Our intake team handles the details. Call or fax to get a referral started — we take it from there.

ways.title: Phone or fax — whichever fits your workflow.
ways.callBody: Speak directly with our intake team. We will confirm receipt, answer questions, and begin the coordination process right away.
ways.faxBody: Send orders, face sheets, or clinical notes to our secure fax line. We confirm receipt and follow up the same business day.

next.title: What to expect after you refer.
next.step1: We reach out to the patient or family — usually within one business day of receiving the referral.
next.step2: We verify insurance benefits and eligibility at no cost.
next.step3: We work with the patient's physician to build an individualized plan of care.
next.step4: A skilled clinician completes the initial home visit.
next.step5: We share progress notes with the referring provider to keep your team informed.

who.title: We work with the whole care team.
who.card1Body: Primary care physicians and specialists can initiate a referral by phone or fax. We handle prior authorization and benefit verification.
who.card2Body: Hospital discharge planners can coordinate directly with our intake team to arrange home care before the patient leaves the facility.
who.card3Body: Insurance and community case managers can refer patients and receive regular updates on progress and plan-of-care changes.
who.card4Body: Family members may initiate a referral inquiry. We will confirm clinical eligibility and coordinate with the treating physician.

hero.headline: Daily check-ins, without leaving home.
hero.intro: Connected home devices track your vital signs every day. A nurse reviews the data and responds before a small change becomes a bigger problem.

advantages.title: Why monitor from home.
advantages.card1Body: Daily readings help our nurses notice a shift in your blood pressure, oxygen level, or weight early, when it is often easier to address.
advantages.card2Body: When changes are caught early, many issues can be handled at home. That may reduce emergency visits and hospital stays.
advantages.card3Body: Ongoing clinical oversight lets you keep living independently in familiar surroundings, with a professional safety net always present.
advantages.card4Body: Readings flow directly to our nurses. If something looks off, we reach out. You are never watching alone.
advantages.card5Body: Loved ones can rest easier knowing a professional team is keeping watch between visits.
advantages.card6Body: Daily data helps your care team fine-tune your plan, which may help keep things steadier over time.

who.title: People who benefit from closer watching.
who.card1Body: Heart failure, COPD, diabetes, and high blood pressure all benefit from steady, day-to-day oversight.
who.card2Body: The weeks after a hospital discharge can be a fragile time. Monitoring helps bridge the gap between the hospital and home.
who.card3Title: Living alone or aging in place
who.card3Body: When no one is nearby to notice a change, connected monitoring becomes a constant, watchful presence.
who.card4Body: Track recovery vitals at home and flag complications early, without repeated trips back to the clinic.

coverage.title: Often covered — we find out for you.
coverage.body: Remote patient monitoring is often covered by Medicare. It may also be available through Texas Medicaid and certain plans. We verify your benefits at no cost and no obligation before anything begins.
coverage.note: Eligibility is determined individually. Call us and we will walk you through your options.

hero.headline: Care that's open to everyone.
hero.intro: Every patient, family member, and referring provider should be able to use this site, whatever tools they rely on. We build with that in mind and keep improving.

commitment.title: We aim to meet WCAG 2.1 AA.
commitment.body: We work to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA — the widely used standard for accessible web design and the benchmark referenced under the Americans with Disabilities Act. Conformance is an ongoing process, not a one-time certification.

done.title: Accessibility measures in this site.
done.item1: A skip-to-content link at the top of every page lets keyboard users bypass navigation.
done.item2: Semantic HTML landmarks and a clear heading structure help screen readers orient users.
done.item3: All interactive elements are keyboard operable, with a visible focus outline.
done.item4: Animations respect the system "reduce motion" preference.
done.item5: Meaningful images include descriptive text alternatives.
done.item6: Colors are chosen with readable contrast in mind.

ongoing.title: Accessibility is never finished.
ongoing.body: We continue to review and improve as we build. If any part of this site is hard to use, tell us and we will work with you to get you what you need.

contact.title: Hit a barrier? We want to help.
contact.body: Reach our team directly. Let us know the page and what got in your way, and we will respond as quickly as we can.
